Team — forwarding Samir's proposal. We have three active vendor conversations (GitHub, Atlassian, JetBrains) that converge in mid-Nov. Procurement asked for a single set of negotiation priorities so we can push for a consolidation discount rather than separate renewals. My initial asks: 

1) Prioritize SSO/SCIM and audit-log export for security — non-negotiable.
2) Maximize multi-product discount threshold (we should push to 20% if we commit to all three vendors for 12 months).
3) Prefer 12-month terms with a single annual true-up date (we want predictable renewal cadence for budgeting).
4) No auto-renew without 60-day written notice and opt-out window.

Can you each weigh in on seat counts and any platform-specific constraints? Ben — can you confirm whether platform infra owns the JetBrains floating license pool today? Karthik — procurement constraints / preferred legal redlines? Neha — any budget limits for Q1 '27? I attached the consolidation RFP we circulated last month for context.

Thanks,

Grace / Team,

Quick procurement readout after reviewing the three vendor documents:
- Budget: finance signaled a hard cap of $420k for Q1 renewals unless we reclassify some spend from OPEX to committed reserved capacity (not likely).
- Seat counts: engineering + platform + data science = ~290 seats total. JetBrains floating licenses currently managed by platform (Ben), but JetBrains requires an administrative owner for license allocation — Ben please confirm the count by Monday.
- Legal redlines: we should push back on auto-renew default and shorten termination notice to 30 days for pilot pools; for enterprise licenses we can accept 60 days. Also add a simple data-handling clause for audit logs retention (45 days) — this matches our SOC2 profile.

Negotiation plan: prioritize getting GitHub and Atlassian into a single channel bundle (Samir + Lara) to hit 18–20% combined discount. For JetBrains we have less leverage price-wise; instead request flexible seat reassignment and annual true-up to avoid mid-year surprises.
